title: Built a trading bot store with my Muse. Looking for honest feedback.
author: No-Limit-4804

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: printing "still under water after fees" on the front page is the most believable thing I've seen a bot seller do. a board total can hide that most single patterns have twenty trades behind them, so I'd put the count next to each one.

replies.author: No-Limit-4804
replies.body:
Done. The counts are on the record page now, tier by tier: Strong 179 trades, Good 20, Lean 3, Coin Flip 4, each with its money line under all three scorings, and they add back up to the board totals.

You called the exact number on the Good tier, twenty trades. The thin ones stay printed too. A count of 3 tells its own story, and hiding it would undo the whole point of the page.

Appreciate the push. This is the kind of feedback that actually changes the product.  [tradersb.com](http://tradersb.com)

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: that's the version I'd trust. Strong at 179 is basically the whole board, so the 27 in the other tiers can't move the total much either way. the useful test now is whether Strong alone stays positive under the harshest of your three scorings.

replies.author: No-Limit-4804
replies.body:
Good test, and I appreciate you running it. Short answer is no, Strong does not stay positive under the harshest scoring. It is actually its toughest line of the three.

Taker: 176 calls, won 77.8%, minus $5.50 total.  
Maker at max price: 175 filled, won 78.3%, minus $4.86.  
Strict post-only: 109 of the 176 filled, won 70.6%, minus $8.36, about minus 7.67 cents a contract.

What stands out to me is that strict does not just fill less, it fills worse. Sixty seven calls never got filled, and the win rate on the ones that did drops about seven points. Looks a lot like adverse selection: at a post-only max price, you tend to get filled right when the market is moving against the call.

So the tier carrying the board is also the one strict execution punishes most. It is all in the same table on the record page, nothing tucked away. And you are right that it is the line to watch: if the trigger ever earns its keep, strict Strong is the first place it will show.

Keep the hard questions coming. They have already made the page better once.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: post-only coming out worst is the usual tell: the orders that never filled were probably the ones the market ran away from, so you only get filled when it's moving against you. I'd put that line first on the page, it's more convincing than any green number.

replies.author: No-Limit-4804
replies.body:
That is exactly how we read it too. The 67 that never filled are not random misses. They are the calls where the price ran off and left the order standing there, and the fills you do catch tend to be the moves coming back at you.

Fair point on the ordering too. Every seller page leads with its kindest number. Leading with the strict one says something else entirely, and it happens to be the truth of how this trades
